text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

White sugar futures in London closed easier across the board reflecting a larger than expected EU tender award and sluggish performance from New York. A total of 58,700 tonnes of current series white sugar received export rebates of a maximum ECU 41.628 per 100 kg at the EU's tender on July 2. August lost $2.90 to close at $319.00 per tonne, while October gave up $2.20 to close at $315.00 per tonne.

Raw sugar futures in New York posted sharp losses after fund selling eroded nearby support and pressured benchmark October to a recent low. October lost 19 points to close at 11.05 cents/lb. March closed 10 points easier at 11.21 cents/lb. The outer months lost between 12 and 14 points. Sluggish end-user demand continues to weigh on prices.

BELGIUM-LUXEMBOURG - Sugar imports in February 1997 amounted to 29,385 tonnes, down from 55,513 tonnes in January and also below the 34,998 tonnes imported in February 1996. This brought cumulative imports in the first five months of 1996/97 (October/February) up to 405,720 tonnes, against 437,329 tonne in 1995/96. Total imports in 1995/96 reached 711,840 tonnes compared to 1.139 million tonnes in 1994/95. Major countries of origin in 1996/97 were France with 275,786 tonnes whites against 339,989 tonnes and Germany with 90,921 tonnes, up from 25,923 tonnes.

Sugar exports in February 1997 amounted to 113,010 tonnes, up from 61,229 tonnes in February 1996. This brought cumulative exports in October/February 1996/97 up to 659,739 tonnes compared to 656,299 tonnes in 1995/96. Total exports in 1995/95 reached 988,722 tonnes, down from 1.566 million tonnes in 1994/95. Major countries of destination in 1996/97 were Syria with 117,830 tonnes whites against 115,248 tonnes, Algeria with 39,654 tonnes, up from 4,252 tonnes, Israel with 39,149 tonnes against 73,645 tonnes and Saudi Arabia with 32,860 tonnes, down from 48,892 tonnes.

NORWAY - Sugar imports in May 1997 amounted to 15,891 tonnes, raw value, up from 14,483 tonnes imported in May 1996. This brought cumulative imports in January/May 1997 up to 71,413 tonnes against 70,742 tonnes in 1996. Total imports in 1996 reached 188,832 tonnes against 173,712 tonnes in 1995. Major countries of origin in 1997 were Denmark with 33,112 tonnes whites against 44,026 tonnes and the United Kingdom with 19,220 tonnes, up from 17,030 tonnes.

INDIA - M.S. Marathe, executive director of the National Federation of Cooperative Sugar Factories Ltd, said that 1997/98 sugar production is expected to fall from this season's 13 million tonnes, white value. However, he gave no precise figure and said that a good monsoon rain will lead to a marginal fall in output while it must be expected falling sharply if the rains are bad. However, he said irrespective of the monsoon performance, output will be low because of a shift in cultivation to other crops.

Industry sources in India believe that even if production should fall sharply, the country will not come onto the world market for larger quantities, due to the high level of stocks. It was added that stocks at the end of 1996/97 (October/September) could total 7.0 million tonnes, white value, still up from the 2.5 million tonnes seen at the end of 1993/94. This could mean that inspite of falling production India could remain a net exporter next season, while the international trade partly expects large Indian purchases next year.

AUSTRALIA - According to preliminary figures, sugar exports in May 1997 amounted to 220,759 tonnes compared to 42,256 tonnes in May 1996. This brought total exports in 1996/97 (June/May) up to 4.327 million tonnes compared to 4.177 million tonnes in 1995/96 and 4.479 million tonnes in 1994/95. Major countries of destination in 1996/97 were Canada with 738,271 tonnes raws against 634,529 tonnes, South Korea with 657,763 tonnes against 605,695 tonnes, Malaysia with 614,558 tonnes compared to 602,925 tonnes and Japan with 607,569 tonnes, down from 706,819 tonnes.

The European Union awarded 58,750 tonnes of white sugar at a maximum refund of ECU 41.628 per 100 kg at its weekly tender on July 2. Cumulative awards so far made under the 1996/97 series of tenders for the period up to July 2 reached 2,348,825 tonnes, which compares to 2,502,448 tonnes last year.
